metadata.name: spl_token_forwarder
metadata.description: SPL Token forwarder for wrap/unwrap operations with Ed25519 signature verification

instructions.name: close_config
docs: Close the config PDA; its rent goes to the owner, who signs. Call
last. Requires the adapter to be paused.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The owner, who receives the config's rent.

instructions.name: close_escrow
docs: Drain a mint's escrow to the recipient and close the escrow token
account; its rent goes to the owner, who signs. Requires the adapter
to be paused.
The closing instructions recover the rent of the forwarder's
accounts, which EVM storage does not hold: they have no EVM
counterpart. The owner holds them because the owner can already
replace the program's code (`upgrade`), as the EVM forwarder's owner
can replace its implementation; the paused adapter keeps them from
running under live settlements.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The owner, who receives the closed escrow ATA's rent.

instructions.name: close_nonce_bitmaps_batch
docs: Close the nonce bitmaps passed as remaining accounts; their rent goes
to the owner, who signs. Requires the adapter to be paused.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The owner, who receives the closed bitmaps' rent.

instructions.name: forward_call
docs: Forward a wrap or unwrap call from the Protocol Adapter, returning
the empty output, as the EVM ERC20 forwarder's `_forwardCall` does.
Like the EVM V2 `ForwarderBaseUpgradeable.forwardCall()`, this does not check the
adapter's paused state: the adapter does not call forwarders while paused.

instructions.name: init_migration_record
docs: Create the migration record of the resource with `nullifier`, paid by
whoever signs, unless it exists, when it does nothing. Permissionless,
as `init_nonce_bitmap`: the record holds nothing but whether the
resource migrated, and a migration requires it to exist, since the
adapter forwards no signer that could pay for it.

instructions.name: init_nonce_bitmap
docs: Create the nonce bitmap for one 256-nonce word of `user`, paid by
whoever signs, unless it exists, when it does nothing. Permissionless:
the bitmap holds nothing but used bits, and a wrap requires it to
exist. The adapter forwards no signer to a forwarder, so the account
cannot be created during the wrap itself; a submitter sends this
instruction ahead of every wrap's settlement, and needs not read the
chain to know whether the bitmap is there. An existing bitmap keeps
its bits: only its bump, the canonical one it already holds, is
written.

instructions.name: initialize
docs: Initialize the forwarder config, owned by `initial_owner`.
As the EVM V2 forwarder's initializer: the owner set (the zero key
refused) and announced, no zero adapter or logic ref. Signed by the
program's upgrade authority, the deployer, which it hands to the
program's upgrade authority PDA, so from then on only `upgrade`, for
the owner, upgrades the program.

accounts.name: program
docs: This program, which the `Initialized` event's self-invocation needs.

accounts.name: program_data
docs: This program's ProgramData, where the loader records the upgrade
authority: the deployer, who alone initializes the forwarder and
hands the authority to `upgrade_authority`.

accounts.name: upgrade_authority
docs: seeds pin it.

instructions.name: reinitialize
docs: The emergency-migrating build's `reinitialize`, as the EVM draft's
`reinitialize(newLogicRef, vulnerableLogicRefs)`: once, after the
owner upgrades the forwarder in place to this build, the owner lists
the vulnerable logic refs, at least one, each denied on both of the
adapter's denylists, and sets the logic ref, on neither, or keeps it.
Emits `VulnerableLogicRefListed` per ref, `LogicRefReplaced` when the
logic ref changes, then `Initialized`.

accounts.name: vulnerable_logic_refs
docs: until the first incident's `reinitialize` creates them, which grows
them at every later one.

accounts.name: pa_state
docs: config's adapter.

instructions.name: renounce_ownership
docs: Give up the ownership for good. Mirrors OwnableUpgradeable's
`renounceOwnership`: owner only; the owner becomes the zero key, so
no owner-only instruction, `upgrade` and `reinitialize` included, can
run again.

instructions.name: transfer_ownership
docs: Move the ownership to `new_owner`. Mirrors OwnableUpgradeable's
`transferOwnership`: owner only, effective at once, the zero key
refused (`OwnableInvalidOwner`), announced with `OwnershipTransferred`.

instructions.name: upgrade
docs: Replace this program's code with the code in `buffer`, as the
adapter's `upgrade`. Mirrors the UUPS `upgradeToAndCall` the EVM
forwarder's owner calls (`_authorizeUpgrade`, owner only), announced
with `Upgraded`, which names the new code by its executable hash. The
buffer's authority must be the owner, who wrote it; the program hands
it to its upgrade authority PDA, which signs the upgrade, and its rent
goes to `spill`. The new code runs from the next slot.

accounts.name: program_data
docs: address pins it.

accounts.name: upgraded_program
docs: the address pins it.

accounts.name: buffer
docs: loader requires to be the owner, who signs; `executable_hash` refuses
any other account.

accounts.name: upgrade_authority
docs: the seeds pin it.

instructions.name: version
docs: The release this build is. Mirrors the EVM forwarder's `VERSION`:
read from the deployed program (by simulation), it names the code an
address runs, which an in-place upgrade changes.

types.name: Config
docs: Configuration account for the forwarder.
The adapter and logic ref mirror the EVM V2 forwarder's
`ForwarderBaseUpgradeable` state, `version` its `Initializable` version,
and `owner` its `OwnableUpgradeable` owner.

fields.name: protocol_adapter
docs: The Protocol Adapter program ID that can call forward_call

fields.name: logic_ref
docs: The logic reference (verifying key) this forwarder handles

fields.name: version
docs: The version the config was last initialized at, as OpenZeppelin
Initializable's `_initialized`: `initialize` records CONFIG_VERSION,
and `reinitialize` raises it to CONFIG_VERSION once.

fields.name: owner
docs: The forwarder's owner, as the EVM V2 forwarder's OwnableUpgradeable
owner: it upgrades the program (`upgrade`), rotates the logic ref
(`reinitialize`), and moves or renounces the ownership. The all-zero
key once renounced, which no one can sign for.

types.name: Initialized
docs: Mirrors OpenZeppelin Initializable: `event Initialized(uint64 version);`

types.name: LogicRefReplaced
docs: Mirrors EVM: `event LogicRefReplaced(bytes32 indexed previousLogicRef,
bytes32 indexed newLogicRef);`

types.name: Migrated
docs: Mirrors EVM: `event Migrated(address indexed token, bytes32 indexed
vulnerableLogicRef, bytes32 indexed nullifier);`. A migration moves no
tokens, so an indexer adding up the `Wrapped` and `Unwrapped` amounts must
not count it.

types.name: MigrationRecord
docs: Whether the resource with a nullifier migrated, as the EVM draft's
`_isNullifierMigrated`. The adapter forwards no signer to a forwarder, so
a migration cannot create this account: the permissionless
`init_migration_record` creates it beforehand, as `init_nonce_bitmap`
creates a wrap's bitmap, and a migration sets `migrated`.
Seeds: ["migration_record", nullifier].

fields.name: bump
docs: The canonical bump of the record's address, stored by
`init_migration_record`.

types.name: NonceBitmap
docs: One 256-nonce word of a user's wrap nonces (Permit2's bitmap pattern).
Seeds: ["nonce_bitmap", user, word_index_le_bytes]. Created by anyone
through `init_nonce_bitmap`, which pays its rent and leaves an existing
bitmap as it is; a wrap only reads and sets bits, so no signer reaches the
forwarder through the adapter's CPI.

fields.name: bump
docs: The canonical bump of the bitmap's address, stored by `init_nonce_bitmap`.

types.name: OwnershipTransferred
docs: Mirrors OpenZeppelin Ownable: `event OwnershipTransferred(address indexed
previousOwner, address indexed newOwner);`. The zero key stands for no
owner: the previous owner when `initialize` sets the first one, the new owner when `renounce_ownership` gives it up.

types.name: Unwrapped
docs: Mirrors EVM: `event Unwrapped(address indexed token, address indexed to, uint128 amount);`

types.name: Upgraded
docs: Mirrors ERC1967: `event Upgraded(address indexed implementation);`, the
new code named by its executable hash, as the adapter's `Upgraded`.

types.name: VulnerableLogicRefListed
docs: Mirrors EVM: `event VulnerableLogicRefListed(bytes32 indexed logicRef);`

types.name: Wrapped
docs: Mirrors EVM: `event Wrapped(address indexed token, address indexed from, uint128 amount);`

constants.name: CONFIG_VERSION
docs: The config version the emergency-migrating build reinitializes to: one
more than the production build it upgrades, as the EVM draft's
`reinitializer(2)` is one more than `ERC20Forwarder.initialize`'s
version, so its `reinitialize` runs once.

constants.name: ESCROW_SEED
docs: Seed of the escrow authority.

constants.name: LEGACY_FORWARDER
docs: The legacy SPL token forwarder of the cluster, whose resources can
emergency-migrate too because its balances moved to this forwarder, or
the zero key on a cluster without one, as the EVM draft's
`LEGACY_FORWARDER`. It comes from env/<cluster>.env, as the EVM draft's
constructor argument comes from the chain's deployment record.

constants.name: MIGRATION_RECORD_SEED
docs: The seed of a migrated resource's record, one per nullifier.

constants.name: NONCE_BITMAP_SEED
docs: Nonce bitmap PDA, one per user per 256-nonce word.

constants.name: OP_MIGRATE
docs: The op byte of a `forward_call` input that migrates resources, after
`OP_WRAP` and `OP_UNWRAP`, as the EVM draft's call type `Migrate`.

constants.name: OP_WRAP
docs: Operation codes, the first byte of a `forward_call` input.

constants.name: VULNERABLE_LOGIC_REFS_SEED
docs: The seed of the vulnerable logic refs' account.
